skills.name: Cells: prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; the cell theory

note.text:
The cell is the basic unit of structure and function of all living things.
Cell theory: (1) all living things are made of one or more cells; (2) the cell is the basic unit of life; (3) all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Two types of cell:
• Prokaryotic (bacteria): small (about 1–10 µm), no true nucleus (DNA lies free in the cytoplasm), no membrane-bound organelles, small ribosomes.
• Eukaryotic (plants, animals, fungi, protoctists): larger (10–100 µm), a true nucleus with a nuclear membrane, membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.
Sizes: 1 mm = 1000 µm. Real size = image size ÷ magnification.

sections.heading: The unit of life
Two kinds of cell
sections.text:
• Prokaryotic cells (bacteria) are small. Their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm: there is no true nucleus. They have no membrane-bound organelles.
• Eukaryotic cells (plants, animals, fungi, protoctists) are larger. Their DNA is inside a nucleus surrounded by a nuclear membrane, and they contain organelles such as mitochondria.
'Pro' means before and 'karyon' means nucleus: prokaryotes came before the nucleus.

sections.heading: How big are cells?
sections.text:
Cells are measured in micrometres: {1} mm = {1000} µm. Most bacteria are {1}–{10} µm long; most plant and animal cells {10}–{100} µm.
In a drawing or photograph: real size = image size ÷ magnification. A cell drawn {50} mm long at ×{400} is really {0.125} mm = {125} µm long.

key_words.meaning: an organism whose cells have no true nucleus (bacteria)
an organism whose cells have a nucleus

examples: Onion epidermis cell: eukaryote, about {100} µm

mistake.why: The drawing is magnified, so the real cell is smaller: divide.

worked_example.problem: A drawing of a cheek cell is {img} mm long at a magnification of ×{mag}. Find the real length of the cell in µm.
steps: Real size = image size ÷ magnification = {img} ÷ {mag} = {realSize(img, mag)} mm.
{1} mm = {1000} µm, so the cell is {realSize(img, mag) * 1000} µm long.

cards.idea: All living things are made of cells, and cells come from other cells.
example: A new skin cell forms when an old one divides.

cards.idea: Prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus; eukaryotic cells do.
example: Bacteria are prokaryotes; you are made of eukaryotic cells.
Image {20} mm at ×{100}: real size {0.2} mm = {200} µm

check.prompt: A cell's image is {img} mm long at magnification ×{mag}. What is its real length in micrometres (µm)?

misconceptions.explain: That is in millimetres. {1} mm = {1000} µm.
Divide by the magnification: the real cell is smaller than the drawing.

pick.q: Which is a statement of the cell theory?
pick.r: All cells come from pre-existing cells
w: Cells can form from non-living matter
Only animals are made of cells
e: The theory says new cells come only from dividing cells.
Plants, fungi and bacteria are made of cells too.
pick.y: Cells arise only from other cells by division.

pick.q: What is the basic unit of structure and function in living things?
e: Organs are made of many cells.
pick.y: Every living thing is made of one or more cells.

pick.q: Who first named 'cells' after looking at cork?
e: Pasteur worked on germs and vaccines.
Newton worked on forces and light.

pick.q: Which feature is found only in eukaryotic cells?
pick.r: a nucleus with a nuclear membrane
e: All cells have a cell membrane.
pick.y: Prokaryotes have DNA free in the cytoplasm, not in a nucleus.

pick.q: Which organism is made of prokaryotic cells?

pick.r: They have no membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria
w: They are larger than eukaryotic cells
They are found only in animals
